answer_1.quote: In this paper, we propose HYDRASUM -a new summarization architecture that disentangles the different stylistic decisions made by abstractive summarization models from the models weights into an explicit model component.
answer_1.outputs: abstractive summaries with varying style features such as abstractiveness, specificity, length, and readability

answer_2.quote: We measure style along the following summarization-relevant dimensions: 1. Abstractiveness: We follow Grusky et al. (2018) and report two metrics, coverage which denotes the fraction of summary words that are also present in the input, and density which denotes the average length of copied contiguous spans in a summary. Additionally, we report the 2-gram overlap between the generated summary and the input article. 2. Degree of specificity of generated summaries, quantified using the Speciteller tool... 3. Length metrics: We report two metrics for this, absolute length (number of words) of generated summaries, and compression ratio... 4. Readability scores of generated summaries, measured using the Flesch readability ease test. In addition to these style-based metrics, we report Quality, measured by ROUGE scores of the generated summaries with respect to the reference summaries.

answer_4.quote: Following prior work , we conduct human evaluation to measure the quality of generated summaries. For 50 randomly sampled input articles from each dataset, we present MTurk workers with 5 different generated summaries...
answer_4.guideline: Workers were asked to rate each summary along 4 dimensions: relevance, coherence, grammatically and factuality. For the first 3, we ask for a rating on the 5-point Likert scale. Following , we seek binary labels (factual (1) or non-factual (0)) for factuality annotation.
